items.title: PolyShell: Unrestricted File Upload (Active Exploitation)
items.summary: This critical vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary code by uploading a disguised image file containing PHP code via the guest cart API. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on October 27, 2026, due to evidence of active exploitation.

items.title: SessionReaper: Unauthenticated RCE and Customer Account Takeover (Active Exploitation)
items.summary: A critical vulnerability allowing customer account takeover and unauthenticated remote code execution under certain conditions. Mass attacks were detected starting October 22, 2026, with attackers uploading PHP backdoors via a file upload vulnerability that was not fully patched by Adobe.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce | APSB26-153 (includes BlockStrap RCE)
items.summary: This update addresses 11 vulnerabilities, including five critical ones. CVE-2026-103849 (BlockStrap) is a template engine injection allowing unauthenticated arbitrary code execution with a CVSS score of 10.0.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce | APSB26-138
items.summary: This bulletin addresses eight vulnerabilities, six of which are exploitable without authentication, including two stored cross-site scripting flaws. Adobe asks merchants to apply the APSB26-146 hotfix in addition to this update.

items.title: StyleSmuggler: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine (Active Exploitation)
items.summary: This critical vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution by injecting malicious code into Magento's template system via styles properties. Adobe released an emergency hotfix on September 7, 2026, and is aware of active exploitation in the wild.

items.title: Security update available for Adobe Commerce | APSB26-92
items.summary: This update resolves critical, important, and moderate vulnerabilities, including an unauthenticated incorrect authorization flaw (CVE-2026-71362, CVSS 9.1) and two stored cross-site scripting flaws. Successful exploitation could result in security feature bypass, arbitrary code execution, and privilege escalation.
